title: Rabbi Nechunya the Great
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Megillah 28a relates that Rabbi Akiva asked him why he had lived so long. The attendants began beating Akiva, who climbed a palm tree and called out: “Master! If ‘lamb’ is stated, why add ‘one’?” Rabbi Nechunya told them: “He is a Torah scholar; leave him alone.” He answered: “‘One’ means the choicest of the flock.” He then said: “I never accepted gifts, never insisted on my rights, and was generous with my money.”
And from this it somewhat implies that Rabbi Nehunya the Great is not Rabbi Nehunya ben HaKaneh.

notes.text: Hyman cautiously infers that Nechunya the Great differs from Nechunya ben HaKaneh; the distinction remains tentative.
Megillah 28a directly contains Akiva’s question, the attendants, the palm tree and the reply. Hyman’s distinction from Nechunya ben HaKaneh remains only tentative.
